 Critical NJ ANCHOR Deadline Is Here: Make Sure You Get Paid
 The final deadline to apply for property tax relief has come. 
 Jack Slocum , Patch Staff 
 Posted Mon, Nov 2, 2026 at 1:12 pm ET | Updated Mon, Nov 2, 2026 at 1:33 pm ET The final opportunity for New Jerseyans to apply for 2025 property tax relief has arrived. 
 Monday marks the final deadline to apply for ANCHOR relief for the 2025 fiscal year. 
 The ANCHOR program, or the Affordable New Jersey Communities for Homeowners and Renters program, offers tax relief for owners and renters in New Jersey, and this year’s relief is based on residents’ 2025 income, age, and residency.

 Most eligible residents had their application re-filed automatically for them. Those new to the program, and people 65+ years old who collect Social Security disability benefits, have to file an ANCHOR application on their own by Monday.

The application allows people to claim benefits from Senior Freeze, ANCHOR, and the Stay NJ Program, all at once, even if they aren't eligible for all of the programs.
 More: Next ANCHOR Tax Rebates Arrive As New Deadline Looms 
 Applicants should prepare their 2025 property tax details, including their County/Municipality Code, Block/Lot/Qualifier, and tax amounts, as well as the gross income reported on their 2024 NJ-1040 when applying.
 To file your ANCHOR application yourself, click here. Remember: these need to be filed by 11:59 p.m. Monday, according to the Division of Taxation. 
 Do I Qualify For ANCHOR? 
 See ANCHOR eligibility requirements below:
 Homeowners are eligible if: 
 You were a New Jersey resident in 2025
 You owned and occupied a home in New Jersey that was your principal residence (main home) on Oct. 1, 2025; and
 Your home was subject to property taxes, and
 Your 2025 New Jersey gross income was not more than $250,000.
 Renters are eligible if: 
 You were a New Jersey resident in 2025
 You rented and occupied a residence in New Jersey that was your principal residence (main home) on Oct. 1, 2025
 Your name was on the lease or rental agreement
 You paid rent
 The rental property was subject to local property taxes
 Your 2025 New Jersey gross income was not more than $150,000.
 Those who have their ANCHOR application re-filed automatically by the state should have received their ANCHOR confirmation letter in the mail already.
 The rebate amounts will be the same as last year’s: $450 for renters to $1,500 for homeowners. Senior homeowners can receive up to $1,750, and senior renters can receive up to $700, depending on income.
 The first payments went out in September on a rolling basis, usually within 90 days of filing. Those who file by paper will only be able to receive their funds by paper check. Online filers have the option to receive a check or to use direct deposit.
 Residents can check their ANCHOR benefit status online here .
